I am a 42-year-old woman farming in Dongfu village, Anzhai township. My family has about 7 mu of good flat land, all irrigated from the village well. I finished junior middle school, which is more than my mother had, and I have been making the farm decisions for over 15 years now. Everyone around here grows winter wheat followed by summer maize — it is the only system that really makes sense on the North China Plain, and it is what I know how to manage.

My wheat went into the ground last October, and right now it is greening up. I will topdress it with urea at jointing stage and again if it looks weak at flag leaf. I irrigate four times for the wheat — one winter irrigation to protect against the cold, and three more in spring and early summer before harvest in early June. For weeds and pests, I spray about four times total: herbicide once, insecticide twice when the aphids come, and fungicide once before heading. I use improved wheat seeds from the local supply shop and rotary tillage before sowing. After I cut the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — Nongda or Denghai, the same varieties my neighbors use. I do no-tillage for the maize because there is no time to waste between wheat harvest and maize sowing; direct seeding works fine. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate twice during the summer, which is usually enough if the rains cooperate. I spray pesticides four times on the maize too — herbicide, insecticide for corn borers, and plant growth regulator to prevent lodging. I do not gamble on cotton or vegetables; the wheat-maize rotation gives me steady grain I can sell or feed, and I understand every step of it.
